title: Who was Yasser Arafat?
hay: who was yasser arafat, and how did palestinians mark the 22nd anniversary of his death this week? the plo chairman and first palestinian president died on 11 november 2004; a wreath was laid at his ramallah tomb on wednesday. anniversary ramallah analysis

title: Red Crescent: infections rising after Gaza floods
hay: red crescent official warns of rising infections in gaza as sewage mixes with floodwater in camps the red crescent's bashar murad says about 70,000 tents were flooded and respiratory infections and meningitis cases are increasing. health gaza strip gaza

title: More than 100 vehicles burned in village south of Nablus
hay: settlers set fire to a scrapyard in al-lubban ash-sharqiya, burning more than 100 vehicles and olive trees wafa reports that dozens of settlers torched a scrapyard, cars and olive trees in al-lubban ash-sharqiya; losses exceed one million shekels. settler violence al-lubban ash-sharqiya west bank

title: London Palestine Film Festival opens at the Barbican
hay: london palestine film festival opens friday with 27 screenings, from gaza testimony to a jenin projectionist the festival runs 13-27 november across london venues, opening at the barbican with the uk premiere of 'who is still alive'. film london diaspora

title: Qalqilya protests plan to close UNRWA hospital
hay: qalqilya residents rally in hospital courtyard against unrwa plan to close the 63-bed facility protesters want unrwa to keep its qalqilya hospital, open since 1951 and serving more than 17,000 refugee families, and reopen two wards. health qalqilya west bank

title: Two Old City youth institutions closed in five days
hay: two old city institutions shut in five days: a sports club closed and burj al-laqlaq sealed again israeli police closed the sons of jerusalem club on 5 november and renewed a six-month closure of the burj al-laqlaq society on 10 november. civil society old city jerusalem

title: Why are 150,000 tents still waiting outside Gaza?
hay: why are 150,000 winter tents sitting outside gaza while families sleep in flooded shelters? aid agencies say entry restrictions, slow approvals and a $186.5 million funding gap keep shelter supplies outside while stocks inside run out. shelter gaza strip gaza

title: Sand cliff collapse kills five in Deir al-Balah camp
hay: five people, three of them children, die as rain-soaked sand cliff collapses on tents in deir al-balah a sand cliff loosened by rain fell on tents at a deir al-balah displacement site on 8 november, killing five people including three children. displacement deir al-balah gaza

title: Masafer Yatta: teachers detained, school raided
hay: in masafer yatta, ten teachers held for five hours on the way home and a school raided a week later the un says ten jinba school teachers were detained for about five hours on 1 november; a teacher was arrested at al-fakhit school on 8 november. education masafer yatta west bank

title: First winter storm swamps Gaza's displacement sites
hay: first winter storm floods displacement sites across gaza, damaging more than 23,000 family shelters ocha says rain from 6 november destroyed over 6,000 family shelters, damaged 17,400 more and left 3,900 households with none. winter storm gaza strip gaza

title: Five solidarity actions, from Stockholm to New Jersey
hay: from stockholm's odenplan to the port of elizabeth: five solidarity actions of the past three weeks marches in stockholm, chicago, berlin and hanover, a port protest in new jersey and a cross-country us convoy all called for an end to arms flows. marches stockholm solidarity

title: Olive harvest in numbers: a record 377 settler attacks
hay: the olive harvest in numbers: 377 settler attacks since september, more than any season on un record ocha counted 377 harvest-related settler attacks between 1 september and 2 november, more than in any previous olive season it has recorded. olive harvest nablus west bank

title: What is UNRWA, and why is it cutting services?
hay: what is unrwa, and why are refugees in the west bank protesting against cuts to its services? the un agency for palestine refugees faces a shortfall of about $70 million and is weighing layoffs and the closure of its qalqilya hospital. refugees nablus analysis

title: Israel to deport 12 olive-harvest volunteers
hay: israel orders deportation of 12 foreign volunteers detained while helping with olive harvest near ramallah seventeen people were detained in kafr ni'ma on 6 november; five germans, four italians, two canadians and an american were ordered deported. olive harvest kafr ni'ma solidarity

title: Why do Gaza doctors want a birth-defects inquiry?
hay: why are doctors in gaza asking for an independent inquiry into a rise in birth defects? gaza recorded 260 congenital anomalies in nine months of 2026 against 184 in all of 2022, and doctors say the cause has not been established. maternal health gaza strip gaza

title: Six Jerusalem demolitions in a fortnight, case by case
hay: six demolitions in two weeks: the east jerusalem families who lost homes, some by their own hands between 25 october and 6 november at least six demolition cases were reported in and around east jerusalem, four carried out by the owners. demolitions east jerusalem jerusalem

title: How does aid get into Gaza now?
hay: how does aid reach gaza now, and why did the number of trucks fall by more than a quarter in a week? most cargo is offloaded at kerem shalom; the un manifested 466 trucks in the last week of october, 28 per cent fewer than the week before. aid kerem shalom gaza

title: 760 environmental violations logged in West Bank this year
hay: seven figures from the palestinian environment authority's count of 760 violations in the west bank the environmental quality authority says it logged 760 environmental violations by israeli forces and settlers from january to september 2026. environment ramallah west bank

title: What is the E1 plan east of Jerusalem?
hay: what is the e1 plan, and why did a bedouin hamlet's demolition raise alarm that it has begun? e1 is a planned settlement of 3,401 homes between jerusalem and ma'ale adumim; palestinians say demolitions at bir al-maskub mark its start. settlements east of jerusalem jerusalem

title: Why is the UK's top court reviewing the Palestine Action ban?
hay: why has the uk supreme court been asked to rule on the ban on the protest group palestine action? the court heard an appeal on 4-5 november on whether the 2025 ban breaches free expression and assembly rights; judgment is still pending. courts london solidarity

title: Courts refuse to free 14 detained Gaza doctors
hay: israeli courts reject two petitions seeking the release of 14 gaza doctors held without charge physicians for human rights-israel says the 14 doctors, some held for more than two years, include hospital directors and specialists. courts gaza strip gaza

title: AU, OIC and Arab League issue joint call on Palestine
hay: african union, oic and arab league jointly call for israeli withdrawal and second phase of gaza ceasefire meeting in addis ababa, the three organisations called for an end to the occupation, a palestinian state and reopening of all gaza crossings. diplomacy addis ababa solidarity

title: Three Gaza siblings get wheelchairs built for them
hay: 'for the first time i have my own chair': three gaza siblings born without legs receive custom aids anas, mohammad and sujood al-sharif received wheelchairs, writing aids and walking supports made in gaza by the ngo educaid with un funding. disability gaza strip gaza

title: 2,536 dunums near Ramallah declared 'state property'
hay: israel declares 2,536 dunums belonging to three villages north-west of ramallah 'state property' a 3 november declaration covers land of beitillu, al-mazra'a al-qibliya and deir ammar; owners have 45 days to object. land beitillu west bank

title: From cart driver back to pupil at 12
hay: a 12-year-old who drove a cart to feed his family is back in class in deir al-balah, with help a boy who lost his mother in a 2024 strike and left learning to work has returned to school after counselling and family support, ocha reports. education deir al-balah gaza

title: What happened in Hebron's ten-day lockdown?
hay: what happened during israel's ten-day operation in hebron, and what did families find when it ended? from 23 october to 2 november israeli forces sealed two hebron neighbourhoods, displacing more than 3,000 people who are now returning. hebron hebron west bank

title: Greece gives €600,000 to East Jerusalem hospitals
hay: greece commits €600,000 to east jerusalem hospitals as who data show a quarter of patient permits unmet greece signed a €600,000 grant for east jerusalem hospitals on 2 november; who says 76% of patient permit requests were approved this year. health east jerusalem jerusalem

title: What was the Balfour Declaration?
hay: what was the balfour declaration, and why do palestinians still mark its anniversary 109 years on? a 1917 letter in which britain backed a 'national home for the jewish people' in palestine; palestinians date their dispossession from it. history london analysis

title: What is Gaza's 'yellow line'?
hay: what is the 'yellow line' in gaza, and why does the un say people near it keep being displaced? it is the line israeli forces pulled back to under the october 2025 ceasefire; the un says it is shifting west and treated as a kill zone. ceasefire gaza city gaza

title: Bethlehem pupil is runner-up in Arab Reading Challenge
hay: bethlehem tenth-grader ghazal taim takes second place among 40 million in the arab reading challenge ghazal taim, 16, of al-awda secondary school for girls, finished second in the 10th arab reading challenge final in dubai on 29 october. education bethlehem west bank

title: What does the UN report on Palestinian journalists say?
hay: what does the un rapporteur's new report say about the killing and jailing of palestinian journalists? francesca albanese's report says nearly 300 journalists and media workers have been killed in gaza and 80% of its media offices destroyed. press freedom gaza strip analysis

title: Israel bars 23-member delegation from Birzeit conference
hay: israel turns back 23 foreign parliamentarians and academics bound for birzeit university conference a delegation including british mp clive lewis was questioned for hours at the allenby crossing on 27 october and refused entry. academia birzeit solidarity

title: 60 MEPs press EU for sanctions over Hebron closure
hay: sixty members of the european parliament urge emergency eu meeting on sanctions over hebron closure in a letter to eu foreign policy chief kaja kallas, 60 meps called the west bank closure collective punishment and asked for sanctions talks. european union brussels solidarity

title: What did the UN inquiry's October report find?
hay: what did the un commission of inquiry conclude in its october report on the west bank and gaza? the commission found war crimes and crimes against humanity in the west bank and said genocidal acts continue in gaza; israel rejects this. international law new york analysis

title: Ben-Gvir at Al-Aqsa on election eve; Egypt, Qatar protest
hay: ben-gvir enters al-aqsa compound on the eve of israel's election, drawing protests from cairo and doha israel's national security minister entered the al-aqsa compound under guard on 26 october, a day before the vote; egypt and qatar condemned it. al-aqsa al-aqsa mosque compound jerusalem

title: Palestinian Women's Day, in seven numbers
hay: palestinian women's day in numbers: what official statistics say about 2.75 million women and girls for women's day on 26 october, the statistics bureau reported that women head about a quarter of gaza's households and 28,560 are widowed. women ramallah analysis

title: Governorate: tunnels under Silwan are cracking homes
hay: jerusalem governorate says tunnelling under silwan is cracking homes and rewriting the area's history the palestinian jerusalem governorate says excavations beneath wadi hilweh have caused cracks and collapses and serve a selective narrative. heritage silwan jerusalem

title: New book traces the history of Palestinian libraries
hay: new international volume documents the fate of palestinian libraries and archives from 1948 to 1993 'resisting erasure', from library juice press, includes anan hamad's study of palestinian libraries and archives under occupation, 1948-1993. books ramallah diaspora

title: Palestinian kickboxers win eight medals in Tashkent
hay: palestinian kickboxers bring home two golds and six bronzes from the world cup in tashkent abdullah kanaan and mohammad alyan won gold as palestine's 27-strong team took eight medals at the kickboxing world cup in uzbekistan. sport tashkent diaspora

title: Barcelona launches Spain's first Palestine studies chair
hay: university of barcelona launches spain's first academic chair dedicated to palestine studies the ub-fundacions ferrer chair for palestine studies was inaugurated in barcelona with an-najah's sanaa alsarghali taking part. academia barcelona diaspora
